name: Dark Greyish Blue-Violet
lede: Dark Greyish Blue-Violet is a dim, muted violet-blue, ColorHub's library name for a darkened, greyed shade of [[blue-violet]], traced to Ridgway's 1912 color atlas.

sections.title: A darkened, greyed blue-violet
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark greyish" plus the parent color [[blue-violet]] [1]. The library dates the swatch to Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912, plate XXIV, and again places it in the ISCC-NBS Dictionary of Color Names of 1955, in the block for greyish purplish blue [1]. Ridgway's plates survive only as scans of an aged, printed chart, so the hex value is an approximation of the original ink, not a measurement of it [1].

The closest named neighbor on file is [[dusk]], almost indistinguishable from it, with [[azurite-blue]] close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 54 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.23 per cent, as photographed [2]. It is rare before 1900, then rises sharply in the 1910s, nearly eight times that decade's average rate, led by Gustav Klimt and Henri Matisse [2]. Austria and Norway both show it well above their average rates in our sample, consistent with its concentration in early-twentieth-century portraits rather than any earlier period in the archive [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
